message_source_quote: The stance-contrast idea is inspired by Raman et al. (2026, white-bear steering), but the prompt pairs are self-authored (not WSB's directed_modulation items), the injection is at prefix positions only (the original uses all positions up to the read cell), and the prefix-only finding was unanticipated by the original work.
writeup_source_quote: The stance-contrast idea is inspired by Raman et al. (2026). New here: prompt pairs are self-authored (not WSB's directed_modulation items), injection is at prefix positions only, and dose and band were tuned independently. The prefix-only finding — injecting at the chat template is as effective as injecting everywhere — was unanticipated by the original, which reports context-only at 0.16.

rationale: Both documents credit Raman et al. (2026) ('white-bear steering') as the inspiration for the stance-contrast idea and both frame the method as building on it with specific stated differences (self-authored prompt pairs, prefix-only injection, and an unanticipated finding relative to the original's reported context-only result). The write-up additionally claims a third novelty point — that dose and band were tuned independently — which the message does not mention, making the message's account of novelty slightly less complete than the write-up's.
